problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{3})=-\sqrt{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ Given that the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘})+4 & =0 \\ 4\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘}) & =-4 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-{45}^{∘}) & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-{45}^{∘} & =-{45}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={45}^{∘}-{45}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ 2x & =n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & =n\cdot {90}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={0}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={90}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x={180}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x={270}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ 

So, in ascending order, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1}={0}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}={90}^{∘},\,{x}_{3}={180}^{∘},\,{x}_{4}={270}^{∘}.
$$
